correctness.rationale: The delta-sink rank-one resolvent gives f(s)=k/(k+sqrt(v^2+4Ds))*exp((v-sqrt(v^2+4Ds))*L/(2D)). Poisson renewal gives ET=(1-f(r))/(r f(r)) with dimensionless y=sqrt(b^2+rL^2/D)-b. For finite a, expansion of the exact derivative numerator N makes N/y^2 strictly increasing and hence yields one global optimum. The coefficient expansion of N yields fixed-b balances y~b sqrt(2/[a(b-1)]) for b>1 and y~(3/a)^(1/3) at b=1. Under b=1+lambda a^(-1/3), y=t a^(-1/3), the normalized equation converges uniformly on compacts to -2+lambda*t^2+2*t^3/3; root brackets give the unique scaling law, including compact-uniform lambda convergence. For 0<b<1, convergence to a unique positive perfect-absorber optimum follows from the same monotone root equation. The self-contained verifier passed 1,591 bounded checks from this package, but numerical sampling is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: A finite absorption imperfection makes each reset-free encounter potentially unsuccessful even for drift toward the target. The consequence is a strictly positive restart optimum at all finite reactivity where the perfectly absorbing model has a zero-rate region. The newly determined inverse-square-root/inverse-cube-root exponents and universal cubic boundary layer quantify experimentally meaningful control scales and a critical crossover that is not a small numerical refinement or arbitrary parameter slice. This is a motivated structural classification of an existing model.
